title.narrative: Strengthening the resilience of conflict-affected population in Borno via WASH Common Pipeline support and improving access to preventive and curative community-based Nutrition services.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis integrated project aims to address acute malnutrition and address hygiene and sanitation-related concerns via support to the WASH common pipeline improved access to curative services vis -a -vis community-based MIYCF, scaling up of OTP services, Mass MUAC screening, Tom Brown therapy among children (6-59 months) and via approaches that mainstream GBV/PSEA. ltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtThis aligns closely with the priorities outlined in the allocation paper for the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) 2023. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe WASH component aims to enhance access to safe water via water quality testing analysis for chemical and bacteriological contaminations, hygiene promotion via production and distribution of context-friendly and age-appropriate IEC materials (illustrative, animative, visual creative, jingles etc) This project will also support the procurement and prepositioning of WASH NFIs that will be accessed by WASH partners across target LGAs via the Common Pipeline Mechanism (CPM). lt/pgtltpgtThe Nutrition component will focus on preventive and treatment services for acute malnutrition, targeting vulnerable populations such as children under five and pregnant and lactating women. It aims to improve early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition through community-based screening, referral, and therapeutic feeding programs. The project also emphasizes the distribution of essential nutrition supplies and the promotion of appropriate maternal, infant and young child nutrition practices.lt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtThis project targets a total of 250,000 beneficiaries, including 100,000 children, 50,000 pregnant and lactating women, and 100,000 individuals for improved WASH services. By addressing acute malnutrition and inadequate WASH access, we strive to reduce malnutrition rates, prevent waterborne diseases, and enhance the overall well-being of the affected population in the BAY states.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project's objectives, interventions, and approach align closely with the allocation paper's priorities for nutrition and WASH. It addresses the urgent needs identified in the BAY states, providing integrated services that contribute to reducing malnutrition and improving access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene. By promoting localization, collaboration, and community engagement, the project ensures a comprehensive, coordinated, and locally-led response.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough the implementation of this project, we aim to make a significant impact in reducing malnutrition rates, improving WASH conditions, and enhancing the overall well-being of the affected population in the BAY states. The project's alignment with the HRP's allocation paper demonstrates a commitment to achieving the desired outcomes and contributing to the overall objectives of the humanitarian response in Nigeria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
